## What it is

Bazarr finds subtitles in the languages you want for the films and series that Sonarr and Radarr manage, and downloads new ones as they appear ([morpheus65535/bazarr](https://github.com/morpheus65535/bazarr)).

**Licence:** `GPL-3.0` (GitHub licence API). Market class **L2**. There is no license-matrix row yet, so the gate notes that it is not preinstallable on sold boxes until one is added (brief 30 B10). The image is built by linuxserver.io ([linuxserver/docker-bazarr](https://github.com/linuxserver/docker-bazarr), GPL-3.0 packaging): Bazarr publishes no image of its own.

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## Market listing

- Category and sub-tags (docs/design/TAXONOMY.md §1): media: downloads. The sub-tags go into `metadata.tags` once the schema has it.
- Deployment class (TAXONOMY §2): **Market · community** until CI writes a passing scan (contract §9.4), then Market · verified if every check passes.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`), one container, started as UID 1000 in linuxserver's documented non-root mode (this image is marked `nonroot_supported`), with a writable in-memory `/run` for the s6 supervisor. linuxserver's startup script turns on non-root mode only when `/run` is not owned by root, so a small init container creates that directory as UID 1000. No privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped.
- Volume: `bazarr-config` (2 GiB, `/config`).
- Probes: `GET /`.

## First run

Source: [Bazarr wiki](https://wiki.bazarr.media) (Setup Guide).

1. Install Bazarr from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-bazarr`.
2. Forward the port and open http://localhost:6767:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-bazarr port-forward svc/bazarr 6767:6767
   ```
3. Bazarr has no login by default: set one in Settings, General, Security first.
4. Choose languages and subtitle providers, then connect Sonarr and Radarr with their API keys.

## Not done yet

- **Shared media:** Bazarr writes subtitle files next to the video files, so it needs the same media folders as Sonarr and Radarr (`/tv`, `/movies`). Each OneMind app has its own volumes in its own namespace, so those folders are not mounted yet; until shared app storage exists, Bazarr can search but cannot save subtitles beside the videos.
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the web UI is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists.
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is not set (linuxserver documents a separate read-only mode; not tested here).
- Resource figures are OneMind choices; upstream publishes none. Idle memory was measured on a k3s smoke test (arm64, 2026-11-12) and the figures were raised to leave headroom above it. They are checked against real use when the CI smoke test (contract §9.4 check 9) runs.
- `metadata.tier` stays `community` until `sdk/tools/app-gate` in CI writes a passing `scan.json`. `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.

## Why this app is blocked

The CI app gate (`sdk/tools/app-gate`, contract §9.4) computed tier **blocked** for this app on 2026-11-12 (ci-apps run 43212771377, job `gate (bazarr)`). The gateway lists a blocked app in the Market but refuses to install it (§10.3, §11.1). The app is kept, not hidden, and the gate was not weakened. Reasons from that run:

- Vulnerability: `lscr.io/linuxserver/bazarr:v1.6.2-ls372`: GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2 in `certifi` 2026.6.17, fixed in 2026.10.18.
- Licence: GitHub GPL-3.0 matches, but there is no research licence-matrix row, so the app is not preinstallable on sold boxes until one is added (brief 30 B10).
- Passed: ClamAV (0 infected), smoke test (GET / returned 200).

To unblock: move the pins to upstream releases that fix these findings (tags that exist, checked with `crane`), then rerun `sdk/tools/app-gate` (the daily `apps-rescan` workflow does this too). Nothing is bumped to an unverified tag.
